newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on last minute buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on last minute buying.

text.p: Thai stocks overcame several rounds of profit-taking to close with small gains on late foreign buying of large capitalised stocks, brokers said.

"Foreign investors were still active, buying bank and communications stocks. Market fundamentals remained unchanged as investors waited for first quarter earnings especially of finance companies which are due out by April 21," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of SITCA Investment and Securities.
The composite SET index gained 1.27 points to 715.36 on 3.3 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index advanced 0.19 point to 53.74. Declines led gainers 151 to 126.
The SET index moved in a narrow range all day as investors turned selective. Profit-taking, focusing on banks, emerged in the last half hour before speculative buying took over in the last minute.
The index fell to an intraday low of 713.30 but late foreign buying pushed it into the positve zone.
The banking sector dominated activities falling 0.53 percent, followed by the communications counter rising 2.04 percent, and the finance sector slipping 1.11 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list rising one baht to 190, Thai Farmers Bank shed two to 123, Advanced Info surged 10 to 234, and Asia Credit gained one to 98.
Support is seen by some brokers at 705 and resistance at 725 on Wednesday.
